name: FastOG — Dynamic Social Cards & Link Previews for WooCommerce
author: fastog

sections.description:
A shared link with no card is a link nobody clicks. When people share your store or
site on Facebook, X (Twitter), LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Slack or Telegram, those platforms
have to pick an image for the post — and for most sites that’s a generic logo tile,
an unrelated photo, or an empty grey box.

FastOG fixes that. It generates a designed social card for every page type from
your real content, automatically, the moment a link is shared. It works with
WooCommerce for storefront pages — and with plain WordPress alone for your front
page and blog posts:

  • Product pages — product photo, name, live price and sale badge.
  • Product categories — the category image and title.
  • Shop / front page — your brand and tagline.
  • Blog posts — title, excerpt and featured image.

Covers are rendered and cached by FastOG, so your site hosts no generated images. No
storage to manage, no image to re-export every time a price changes.

What you get

  • No manual design work. No Photoshop, no Canva, no designer backlog. Pick a
    starting look in FastOG Studio and covers build themselves from your catalogue.
  • Prices that stay current. Cards are generated from live product data, so a price
    change or a new sale badge shows up on the next share — not on a stale image.
  • Zero impact on your store’s speed. og:image URLs point at FastOG’s cache, so
    social crawlers load them fast without touching your server or eating your bandwidth.
  • Plays nice with your SEO plugin. If Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress
    is active, FastOG hands its cover to that plugin instead of printing a competing tag
    that social crawlers might ignore. One image, one set of tags, no conflict.
  • Works with or without WooCommerce. WordPress alone gets front page and blog post
    covers. Add WooCommerce and product, category and shop pages get theirs too.

Try it free

15-day free trial — no credit card. Connect your site, choose which page types get
a cover, pick a look, and share a link. Every starting look stays editable in FastOG
Studio whenever you want to restyle.

  • FastOG Service Terms: https://fastog.com/terms
  • FastOG Privacy Policy: https://fastog.com/privacy
  • Service Pricing & Plans: https://fastog.com

Which pages get a cover

The four page types above. Every other URL — pages, tags, date and author archives,
custom post types — is left exactly as it was, so your theme or SEO plugin keeps
control of it. FastOG only touches the shares that benefit from a designed card.
sections.installation:
From zero to a shared, designed card in about two minutes:

  1. Upload the fastog-for-woocommerce folder to wp-content/plugins/, or install
    the plugin from the admin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Open FastOG Studio → Setup and follow the three steps: connect this site,
    choose which page types get a cover, and pick a starting look. Activation
    itself contacts nothing — connecting is the step that does.
  4. Open Studio to see the covers. Every starting look stays editable there.

WooCommerce is optional: without it, FastOG covers your front page and blog
posts. Product, product category and shop covers need WooCommerce.

The first FastOG Studio screen shows sample product, sale, collection and shop
covers before connection. These are fictional examples; your catalogue is not
read until you start setup.
sections.faq:
Why do my shared links look generic?

Most stores ship no Open Graph image for product and category pages, so social
platforms fall back to a logo or a blank tile. FastOG prints a designed og:image
for every page type, so every share gets a card worth clicking.

Do I need WooCommerce?

Not for the covers themselves. Without WooCommerce, FastOG covers your front
page and blog posts from WordPress data alone. WooCommerce adds the storefront
page types: product, product category and shop covers read your catalogue, so
those three need it installed and active.

Will this slow down my site?

No. Covers are rendered and cached on FastOG and served from there, so your
server only signs a URL — there are no images generated or stored on your hosting
and no impact on page speed.

I use an SEO plugin. Which one wins?

FastOG does. If Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress is active, we do not
print a competing <meta property="og:image"> — a second one does not override the
first, it competes with it, and social crawlers take the first they find. Instead
your FastOG cover is handed to that plugin, so it prints our image with its own
title, description and URL. Without an SEO plugin, FastOG prints the full set of
Open Graph and Twitter card tags itself.

Does the plugin load external code?

No. The editor’s script and stylesheet are bundled inside the plugin and served
from your own site. The only requests that leave your server are the FastOG API
calls the Studio editor makes when you open it.

When does this send site information to FastOG?

Only after you explicitly choose Start setup. Activation and ordinary
admin page loads do not contact FastOG.

Does this send customer data to FastOG?

No. Only a site-level profile (site name, site URL, WordPress/WooCommerce/PHP
versions and locale) is sent when you connect. No customer, order, or other
personal data is transmitted.

Where are the card images hosted?

On FastOG. og:image URLs point at FastOG, so your site doesn’t need extra
storage or a CDN.

Is there a free trial?

Yes — 15 days, no credit card required. Connect your site and the full setup is
available to try before you decide on a plan. Pricing and plans are at
https://fastog.com.

Do I have to finish setup?

No. Until you finish it, FastOG points Studio and Plan at Setup so nothing
half-configured goes live — and Skip setup for now lifts that immediately.
Tools is never held back: that is where you reconnect or disconnect.

How do I make a changed cover show up?

Cover URLs contain the settings that produced them, so editing a cover produces a
new URL. A page cache can keep serving the old one — press Purge caches on the
FastOG Studio screen.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

Deleting the plugin removes everything it stored on your site, including its access
key, from every site on a multisite network. Your store record and cover images on
FastOG stay in your FastOG account, where you can delete them; covers already
shared in social posts keep working until that record is removed.

I had this installed before the FastOG rename — do I lose my setup?

No. The stored credentials (API key, secret and tier) are migrated automatically,
so there is nothing to re-enter.
